theFix.diffSummary: 123 lines added, 3 changed, in loadLandingAndCad and three new exports (ACCOUNT_CROSSWALK_ROWS_SQL, quickRefIdNumericStem, loadAccountCrosswalk); CAD_ROWS_SQL gains two SELECT columns (property_number, quick_ref_id). theFix.mechanism: loadLandingAndCad now branches on SEED_BLOCKED_FIPS.includes(county) (imported from src/lib/cad-txgio-alias-counts.mjs, not a parallel constant). Non-blocked: byte-identical to before (same CAD_ROWS_SQL call, same Map construction). Gate-blocked: cadByProp is built ENTIRELY by loadAccountCrosswalk, which runs ACCOUNT_CROSSWALK_ROWS_SQL (a JOIN on txgio_parcel.geo_id = cad_property.property_number, ambiguity-guarded by NOT EXISTS, DISTINCT ON node prop_id + latest tax_year -- the same shape as this repo's own PR #144 CADROLL_EXPECTATION_SQL_GATE_BLOCKED, extended to select the full CAD row instead of just checking existence), then applies an app-level quick_ref_id-stem corroboration (quickRefIdNumericStem) mirroring LDT's accountCrosswalkForNode/crosswalkBindCorroborated fail-open-on-absent, fail-closed-on-disagreement rule. A resolved row is stored keyed by the NODE's own prop_id (so every existing cadByProp.get(propId) call site, including the ENGINE_PIN'd vendored parcel-record-engine's ingestCadOntoRecords, works unmodified) but with its OWN prop_id field left as the crosswalked ACCOUNT's prop_id -- so apn and every absent-verified basis correctly name the account actually joined (the CP1-required provenance), never the node's own untrustworthy bare number. A node with no bind, or a disagreeing corroborator, gets no map entry at all: ingestCadOntoRecords' own pre-existing join-miss path (applyCadJoinMiss) then emits honest absent-verified cells -- no new absence mechanism was invented.
theFix.corroborationDirectionCorrectedDuringBui: My own first test run caught a real design mistake before it reached CP2: I initially fixture-tested with quick_ref_id = 'R' + the CROSSWALKED ACCOUNT's own current prop_id (e.g. 'R84639' for node 97658 resolving to account 84639) and the corroboration correctly REFUSED it -- because live production data (verified below) shows Hays' quick_ref_id actually mirrors the NODE's own bare prop_id ('R97658' on account 84639, not 'R84639'), consistent with TxGIO's node numbering having been historically seeded from QuickRefID, a stable field distinct from the CAD roll's current, separately-renumbered PropertyID. Fixed the test fixtures, not the code -- the code already matched accountCrosswalkForNode's documented direction; my first fixture guess did not.
theFix.vendoredEngineNotTouched: src/lib/parcel-record-engine/ (ENGINE_PIN'd, hand-editing forbidden) required zero changes -- ingestCadOntoRecords/applyCadScalar/applyCadJoinMiss all consume cadByProp via .get(propId) only; remapping the Map before it reaches them was sufficient, exactly mirroring how P-177's own tier1-bake fix (effectiveCadPropertyRoll) worked in a different repo.

criticalFindingRequiringDecisionBeforeSt.title: The dispatch's Williamson premise ('no contradictions today but 282,569 phantom nodes') and LDT's own LANDUSE_JOIN_DISABLED_FIPS_SEED comment ('Williamson -- R-account TxGIO ids vs six-digit CAD roll, ~0% owner match') both read as: Williamson's bare-number join is broken/absent, like Hays. Live measurement against PRODUCTION_NEONDB_URL directly contradicts this.

measurement.owner_name_agreement_on_the_bare_join: 304,155 / 304,162 rows = 99.998% (sampled across all tax years; the distinct-node figures above are 282,569/282,570)
measurement.sample: 8 spot-checked rows (R000009, R000013, R000016, R000017, R000019, R000032, R000037, R000038): txgio_parcel.owner_name and cad_property.owner_name IDENTICAL on every single one, situs addresses plausible and specific.

criticalFindingRequiringDecisionBeforeSt.reconciliation: Working hypothesis, not yet fully confirmed: LANDUSE_JOIN_DISABLED_FIPS_SEED's '~0% owner match' likely describes matching TxGIO's R-prefixed ids against cad_property's NUMERIC-roll rows (WILLIAMSON_CROSSWALK_SQL's own numeric_roll CTE -- a DIFFERENT, disjoint slice of cad_property that legitimately lacks the R-account identity), not against cad_property's OWN R-prefixed rows (what my bare join, and CAD_ROWS_SQL, actually match against). If true, Williamson's 'gate-blocked' designation is about a DIFFERENT mechanism (the split-roll dollar/structural recovery, which WILLIAMSON_CROSSWALK_SQL/mergeWilliamsonCrosswalk in this SAME file already handles correctly) than the coincidental-bare-number-collision defect class Hays has and this fix targets. I have not chased this to a fully confirmed root cause -- flagging the measured contradiction plainly rather than asserting a conclusion I have not verified as thoroughly as the Hays side.
criticalFindingRequiringDecisionBeforeSt.consequenceIfUnaddressed: Because Williamson's own geo_id is 100% blank (measured above), loadAccountCrosswalk resolves ZERO accounts for Williamson today. If SEED_BLOCKED_FIPS-driven replacement is executed against real Williamson data via step 3, cadByProp would go from ~282,565 populated, ~99.998%-owner-correct entries to completely empty for the ENTIRE county -- converting essentially all of Williamson's CAD-derived parcel_record cells (situsAddress, dollars, structural, legal) from real values to honest absence in one write. This is a much larger and more consequential change than 'a documented no-op,' which is what my CP1 speculated before I ran this measurement -- CP1's williamsonCaveat was itself incomplete; this supersedes it.
criticalFindingRequiringDecisionBeforeSt.recommendation: Scope step 3's actual re-run to Hays (48209) only. Do NOT execute --apply for county 48491 under this fix until this finding is either (a) confirmed as a misread of LANDUSE_JOIN_DISABLED_FIPS_SEED's own measurement scope (in which case Williamson may need a NARROWER version of this fix, or no change at all, rather than the uniform SEED_BLOCKED_FIPS branch), or (b) the operator explicitly accepts the described consequence. The CODE itself stays county-parameterized via SEED_BLOCKED_FIPS as instructed (never a Hays literal) -- this is a recommendation about which counties step 3 actually WRITES this wave, not a request to special-case the code.
